title: The seven steps
hookLine: a wedding fire, a knotted scarf, stolen shoes, and a guest asking what's actually happening
carry: partners in dharma, friends by the seventh step
last: BHAJAN — BHAKTI BELONGS TO EVERY VOICE.

cards: A wedding hall, hour three. The couple sit under a canopy with a small fire between them and the priest. The groom's scarf has been knotted to the bride's sari.
Two aunts are whispering about which way the knot should go. Near the door, the bride's cousins are hiding the groom's shoes and planning what to charge for them.
And the groom's best friend, who didn't grow up with any of this, leans over and asks: what's actually happening? Plenty of people in that room couldn't tell him. Today: the steps in the middle.

teach.b: The fire is Agni, and in the old wedding rites the fire is the witness. Everything important happens in front of it.
When Sita married Rama, the Ramayana says, her father Janaka placed her hand in Rama's and said: this is Sita, my daughter, your partner in dharma; take her hand in yours.
That's the Hindu idea of marriage in one line: two people walking dharma, the right way to live, together.

In many weddings the couple walk around the fire, often seven times, in some communities four; these circles are the pheras. Inside or beside them is a rite called saptapadi: seven steps, taken together.
An old household manual gives a wish for each step. One for food. Two for strength.
Three for wealth. Four for happiness. Five for the herds, since this is a very old text.
Six for the seasons. And at the seventh: with seven steps, be my friend.
Partners in dharma, and at the last step, friends.
Around it you'll see more, and families do these differently. Kanyadaan, the bride's parents placing her hand in the groom's, as Janaka did, which many families now do differently or reword.

teach.h: AT THE SEVENTH: BE MY FRIEND.
teach.b: A mangalsutra, a necklace of black beads and gold, tied by the groom in many weddings. Sindoor, red powder, drawn into the parting of the bride's hair in many North Indian weddings. And the stolen shoes?
That's joota chupai, a game, not a rite. The ransom is negotiable.

how: In many Hindu weddings the couple circle a sacred fire (the pheras) and take seven steps together (saptapadi) while a priest recites the vows; families differ on the number of circles and on customs like kanyadaan, the mangalsutra and sindoor.

seven steps a couple take together at a wedding
seven days of fasting before a wedding

games.q: what's happening at the wedding — tap the pairs.
p: gave Sita as Rama's partner in dharma

s: every Hindu wedding has exactly seven circles of the fire
many have seven, some communities four; families and regions differ.
at the seventh step the couple are called friends
'with seven steps, be my friend', in an old household manual.
hiding the groom's shoes is one of the sacred rites
it's a game: the bride's side hides them and asks a ransom.

games.q: you're the groom's friend at your first Hindu wedding. the couple have just taken the seventh step together. what's the wish at that step?
o: with seven steps, be my friend.
games.why: one step for food, two for strength, and on up; at the seventh: with seven steps, be my friend.

practice: Seven breaths, seven steps. Think of someone who has walked beside you for a long time: a partner, a parent, a brother or sister, a friend.

With each slow breath, take one step beside them in your mind: food, strength, wealth, happiness, the herds if you like, the seasons. On the seventh breath, just the word: friend, and sit quietly with them for a while.

wordCard.voice: Saptapadi. Seven steps, taken together before the fire, by partners in dharma; at the seventh, the couple are called friends. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: sapta, seven, and pada, step. the seven steps at the heart of many Hindu weddings.

carryVoice: Your line: partners in dharma, friends by the seventh step. The last vow is the plainest one. Day one hundred thirty-seven.

sources.ref: Paraskara Grihya Sutra 1.8.1 (the seven steps: food, strength, wealth, happiness, cattle, seasons, friendship)
